newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse weekly turnover up 144 pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse weekly turnover up 144 pct.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 144 percent surge in its turnover, pushing the BSE short-term debentures index up 86.68 points in the week to August 1.
Traders attributed the increase to a renewed activity by the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) which sold 80 million dinars worth of its short-term bonds.
Total turnover rose to 116.896 million dinars ($19.18 million) in 136 transactions from 47.89 million dinars in 103 deals a week ago. All trade took place on the primary market.
The BSE index of short-term debentures rose 43.51 percent to 285.91 index points from 199.23 ponts a week ago.
Traders said liquidity of the market was good now that some of the hard currency raised after Serbia sold part of its Telecom early in June was converted into dinars.
But most fresh dinar funds remained stuck in banks which seemed reluctant to extend fresh loans. Meanwhile, demand for fresh borrowing was unchanged compared to several weeks ago.
Improved liquidity and a lack of demand pushed interest rates further down to 5.00 percent per month from a monthly 5.5-6.5 percent a week ago.

Apart from the NBY short-term bonds, the rest of the market activity was subdued due to holidays. But analysts cautioned August could be risky for the country's financial system, because the government's liabilities towards farmers mature.
August pay-outs to farmers traditionally cause disturbances in the country's financial system and trigger inflation, analysts said.

"The state must pay farmers for the harvest and for the last year's crop. It may be tempted to do something ahead of the September 21 elections to secure the farmers' votes which could threaten this superficial stability," a trader said.
For the week ending August 1, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 114 deals totalling 31.735 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded five times for a total of 0.786 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between monthly 5.00 and 8.00 percent while maturity stood between seven and 120 days.
* NBY short-term bonds traded five times for a total of 80 million dinars.

The central bank currently sells two tranches of its short-term bonds, one 70 million dinars and another 50 million dinars worth. Both carry a 41.63 percent annual interest. The first tranche matures August 18 and the second on August 28.
Traders criticised the NBY for auctioning its short-term bonds without previous notice and said it seemed that any NBY bond buying was pre-arranged.
* OTC trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 100.32 million dinars from 64.26 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, fell to 26.6 million dinars from 28.3 million a week ago.
NOTE -- The BSE short-term debentures index is calculated on volume, interest rate and maturity of the most frequently bourse-traded short-term commercial paper and treasury bills.
Index base is 1996.
-- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
($1 = 6.0941 Yugoslav dinars)
